Series::cummin¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::cummin() const -> Series
Series::cummin(std::int64_t dim) const -> Series

What It Does¶

cummin() computes a running minimum along one axis — the mirror of cummax().

It is a scan, not a reduction: the axis keeps its full length and each position is replaced by the smallest value seen from the start of the axis up to and including that position.

For a row [5, 3, 4, 1, 2] the running minimum is [5, 3, 3, 1, 1] — it never increases, and it latches onto each new low until a smaller one appears.

The no-argument form scans axis 0. Pass dim to scan a different axis; negative values count from the back.

Parameters¶

dim (std::int64_t, optional)

The axis to scan. Omitted: axis 0. Negative values count from the back. The result keeps the same shape.

Returns¶

Series The running minimum along dim, same shape and dtype as the input (an integer series stays integer).

Gradient¶

cummin() is differentiable.

Its backward routes the sensitivity of each output position to the single input position that held the running minimum there, so a value that stays the low for a long stretch collects the gradient of every output in that stretch. On a tie the earliest position keeps the record, matching the forward.

Examples¶

Example 1. The running minimum of a 1-D row.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({5.0, 3.0, 4.0, 1.0, 2.0}).cummin(0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[5.0000, 3.0000, 3.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000]

Example 2. dim selects the axis.

auto m = pluss::make_series({
    {5.0, 2.0, 4.0},
    {3.0, 6.0, 1.0},
});

std::cout << "dim 0:\n" << m.cummin(0);
std::cout << "\ndim 1:\n" << m.cummin(1);

Output¶

dim 0:
pluss::Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[5, 2, 4],
  [3, 2, 1]]
dim 1:
pluss::Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[5, 2, 2],
  [3, 3, 1]]

Example 3. Integer input keeps its dtype.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({4, 2, 3, 1}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64).cummin(0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[4, 2, 2, 1]

Example 4. The backward sends each output’s sensitivity to the position that held the low.

auto x = pluss::make_series({5.0, 3.0, 4.0, 1.0, 2.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.cummin(0).sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 0, 2, 0]

Position 1 held the low at outputs 1 and 2; position 3 held it at outputs 3 and 4. Positions 2 and 4 were never the low and get 0.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • cummin() is a scan, not a reduction. To collapse the axis to a single minimum, use min().

  • A NaN is skipped by the running comparison rather than propagated.

  • Ties keep the earliest position, in both the output and the gradient.

Summary¶

cummin(x) is the running minimum along an axis:

  • shape- and dtype-preserving scan; default axis is 0

  • monotonically non-increasing along the scanned axis

  • differentiable: each output’s sensitivity flows to the position that held the record, ties to the earliest

See Also¶

  • Series::cummax: the running maximum.

  • Series::min: the whole-axis minimum, which removes the axis.

  • Series::cumsum: the additive prefix scan.
